cards.explanation: The answer is none at all. Jesus is plain about it: if you do your righteous acts to be seen by men, “…you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.” (Matthew 6:1) Zero, friends. That's like stamping out a whole batch and finding out the oven was never on. All that work, nothing coming out warm.

The answer is to be honored by men. That's the reason Jesus gives. The hypocrites give “…to be honored by men.” (Matthew 6:2) The gift is for the needy, but the trumpet is for the crowd. I think that's the loudest way anyone has ever asked for a thank-you.

The word is secret. Jesus says not to let your left hand know what your right hand is doing, “…so that your giving may be in secret.” (Matthew 6:3-4) Quiet giving, no trumpet. It's the kind of gift where even your own other hand is left out of the loop.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.” (Matthew 6:4) No crowd, no trumpet, and He still sees it. The one who matters is watching.

The answer is in the synagogues and on street corners. The hypocrites love to pray “…standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men.” (Matthew 6:5) Synagogues are where people gathered, and street corners are where people walk by. Either way, it's a place with an audience.

The answer is into your inner room. Jesus says, “…go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen.” (Matthew 6:6) The hypocrites pray where people can see. You go where it's just you and the Father.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen.” (Matthew 6:6) The door gets shut, friends. My mustache could probably manage that, but I'd want a practice run.

The first blank is words, and the second is heard. Jesus says the pagans “…think that by their many words they will be heard.” (Matthew 6:7) Their thinking is that more words means more chances of being heard. Jesus tells His listeners not to be like them (Matthew 6:8).

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.” (Matthew 6:8) He knows before a single word is said. That's why Jesus says not to be like the pagans with their many words.
The answer is True. Jesus says to pray like this: “Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.” (Matthew 6:9) It opens by talking straight to the Father. No long speech first, just a simple start.
The answer is False. The prayer says, “…Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.” (Matthew 6:10) Earth is right there in the request, not left out. It asks for God's will here too.

The answer is our daily bread. The prayer says, “Give us this day our daily bread.” (Matthew 6:11) The word is “daily,” and it's for this day. I can respect a prayer that doesn't ask for more than that.

The first blank is forgive, and the second is forgiven. The prayer says, “And forgive us our debts…” (Matthew 6:12) That's a request, asking God to forgive. Then it says, “…as we also have forgiven our debtors.” (Matthew 6:12) Same word family, but the second one is about what we've already done. Easy to mix up, so keep a sharp eye, friends.

The answer is the evil one. The prayer says, “And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.” (Matthew 6:13) That's the last request in the prayer. It's the final thing Jesus has us ask.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours.” (Matthew 6:15) The line right before it says the other side: if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). It's a heavy one, and Jesus doesn't soften it.
The word is men. The hypocrites “…disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting.” (Matthew 6:16) The sad face is for people watching. It's an audience thing again.

The answer is to anoint your head and wash your face. Jesus says, “But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face…” (Matthew 6:17) It's the opposite of the hypocrites disfiguring their faces. The purpose He gives is “…so that your fasting will not be obvious to men…” (Matthew 6:18)

The answer is so your fasting isn't obvious to men. That's the reason Jesus gives. You anoint your head and wash your face “…so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen.” (Matthew 6:18) Men don't have to know. Your Father does.
